$comment: ACCEPTED bytecode drift: deployed addresses whose on-chain runtime code (immutables masked) is NOT reproduced by a clean build of this tree. Every entry needs a reason, because an exemption without one is not a decision. Enforced BOTH ways by bytecode_audit.py --baseline: an un-listed STALE address fails, AND a listed address that has become CURRENT fails so the file cannot rot into a rubber stamp. Delete an entry the moment its address is redeployed - do not leave it 'just in case', because it would then silently accept a FUTURE drift at that address. TWO DISTINCT THINGS ARE LISTED, and the difference matters more than the count. The 23 BridgeEscrowImplementation rows are OUT OF SCOPE by decision (2026-08-27) - accepted, not pursued, and undiagnosed. The single PolygonStakingMeta row is IN SCOPE: a real open item with a known cause, a known display-only impact, and a known fix (redeploy). Do not let the 23 bridge rows make the 24th look routine - check every entry's 'scope' field before appending to this file.
$howToAdd: Run `forge clean && forge build` then `python3 script/deploy/preflight/bytecode_audit.py <chainId>`. Anything reported [STALE] is either something to redeploy or something to declare here. Prefer redeploying.

Do not read this entry as evidence it is harmless. DECLARED ON EVERY CHAIN THAT RECORDS IT: the implementation is CREATE2-deployed from fixed type(BridgeEscrow).creationCode (01_DeployImplementations.s.sol), so all 23 copies live at this one address and share the one mismatch.
